families.name: shared-prefix
families.why: Every candidate is the same prefix value followed by its own tail, so the merged source computes the prefix once and duplicates the value with `dup`: extraction emits one node per shared value. This family is where a content-sharing saving is possible at all.

gates.detail: the oracle gives every candidate the same value in the merged and separate programs
12 candidate outputs and one input in every merged graph
shared 56 live nodes = prefix 18 + tails 38; recomputed 243 live nodes = prefix + 11 further prefix copies + tails
every candidate graph reproduces the oracle value on every row
the merged graph and its recomputing twin reproduce the oracle on every row, and each other
every net candidate and both merged forms agree with the independent oracle and packed evaluator on every frozen row
the reference interpreter agrees with the oracle on the first 256 rows
reference, packed, net and oracle agree on all frozen rows for every separate, merged and recomputing graph
the extraction is byte-identical and the evaluation text is identical when repeated

extraction_timing.note: reported only; extraction is producer work and is not part of any evaluation arm

families.name: distinct-prefix
families.why: Every candidate is an independent program over the one input, with no value common to two candidates beyond the input node itself. Merging cannot remove work here, so the two merged arms are the same program: their difference measures the host's timing noise floor.

gates.detail: the oracle gives every candidate the same value in the merged and separate programs
12 candidate outputs and one input in every merged graph
no candidate shares a value: merged 55 live nodes = the input plus every candidate's own nodes
every candidate graph reproduces the oracle value on every row
the merged graph and its recomputing twin reproduce the oracle on every row, and each other
